intro: Jewelers work with fine detail, serve customers and judge quality by eye, skills used in craft, media and precision trades. The closest of the 25 careers below is Craft Artists, with a 78% skill match, while Sound Engineering Technicians are 67% matched and earn a BLS May 2025 median of $73,130, or 39% more.
why_it_works: Making or repairing jewelry means steady hands, careful measurement and explaining options to customers who care about every detail. O*NET rates coordination, judgment and social perceptiveness at 2.88 out of 5 for this job. Craft, prepress and finishing work use the same detail skills. All 25 matches need no extra education. The gaps are quality analysis and operating equipment.
tips: Camera operators earn $74,990, which is 43% more, and value a precise visual eye.
Layout Workers, Metal and Plastic earn $63,870, or 22% more, and use your metalworking skills.
Learn CAD and 3D printing for jewelry; both raise your value in modern shops.

faq.q: What jobs can former jewelers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Craft Artists (78%), Prepress Technicians and Workers (70%) and Furniture Finishers (67%), based on O*NET 31.0. Fiberglass laminators are also 67% matched and earn $46,880, which is 11% less than the $52,540 jeweler median.

faq.q: Which careers for jewelers pay more?
faq.a: 10 of the 25 matches pay more. Camera operators earn $74,990 (43% more), Sound Engineering Technicians $73,130 (39% more) and metal and plastic layout workers $63,870 (22% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. None of these needs more education.

faq.q: Do jewelers need more education to change careers?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches need no more education than jewelers and precious stone and metal workers already have, including all of the top 10. In a close match, 39% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent, so your craft skills matter more than formal schooling.

The skills that most often need work are operations monitoring, operations analysis, quality control analysis and operation and control. Service orientation already rates 2.62 out of 5 for jewelers in O*NET, so running precision equipment is the main step toward better pay.
